Build a UGC Portfolio Brands Hire From (2026 Tutorial)

A UGC portfolio is a short set of sample videos that show how you film a product. Brand managers open that folder before they look at follower count. You will get a list of clips to include, a weekend filming plan, a quality checklist, and a three-line email to send with the folder.

Last updated: August 2026. The format brands ask for has not changed much: vertical, 15-30 seconds, captions, no watermark. Clean samples matter more than a fancy website.

Need products to film? Use the 50 UGC product ideas checklist. Once the folder is ready, pitch from our list of brands that pay for UGC.

Put These Clips Where Brands Can Find Them

A Drive link in a cold email gets ignored more often than a profile brands already browse. Add your samples to a free newcollab profile so hiring managers can send briefs directly.

📋Table of Contents

1. What a UGC portfolio is
2. The 8 clips brands look at first
3. Pick a niche you can actually film

6. How to package and share the folder

8. FAQ

What a UGC Portfolio Is

Treat it as a showreel of short product videos. Someone on a brand team has 90 seconds. They click two or three files. If lighting, voice, and product visibility are clear, they read your rates. If the files are 4 minutes long, watermarked, or shot in a dark room, they close the tab.

This table is the split most people mix up:

AssetWhat it isWho opens itTime to make
UGC portfolio8-12 vertical sample videosUGC manager, creative producerOne weekend if you film products at home
Media kitOne PDF or page: niche, rates, contactThe same person, after they like a clip30 minutes. See the media kit template.
Instagram or TikTok gridPublic posts, often with watermarks and trendsNice extra. Hard to download for ads.Ongoing. Do not treat it as the portfolio.
newcollab profileSamples + niche in one place brands already searchBrands hiring UGC on the platformSame afternoon you export the files
  • Follower count is optional here. UGC is bought as creative. See UGC vs influencer marketing if you want the full split.
  • You do not wait for PR boxes. Film what you already own, then apply. Paid briefs usually ship product after you are booked.
  • Keep files brands can run in ads. No TikTok watermark, no trending audio you cannot license.

The 8 Clips Brands Look at First

Eight videos that cover how brands cut ads is enough. If a manager can see talking-head, texture, in-use, and a quiet B-roll clip, they can brief you. Fill this table, then stop filming until these eight are exported.

Clip typeWhy they want itLengthExample opening
Talking-head hookShows your face, voice, and first three seconds15-20s"My skin was tight by 3pm until this"
Texture / unbox close-upAds need label and product shots they can cut in8-15sSilent pour, pump, or peel. Logo readable.
Product in a real routineProves you can place the item in daily life20-30s"This is step 3 in my morning"
Problem then resultClosest to how paid ads are structured15-25s"Dry hands, then 20 seconds later"
B-roll only, no talkingSome brands want footage they voice over themselves10-20sHands, product, room. No voiceover.
Honest reviewTrust. Say one thing you like and one limit20-30s"I would buy this again, with one caveat"
On-body / GRWM contextFashion, beauty, and lifestyle briefs ask for this20-30s"Getting ready with the product on me"
Simple close / CTA styleShows you can land a last line without sounding like an ad read5-8s"This stays in my kit."

If you only have time for four, shoot talking-head, texture, in-use, and B-roll. That set covers most first briefs in beauty, home, and CPG.

Pick a Niche You Can Actually Film

A niche here means two product categories you can film this month without buying a studio. Skincare plus home works. Tech plus food works. "Luxury only" does not, if your bathroom is drugstore. Brands care that the lighting and voice match the category they sell.

Niche pairFilm with what you ownTypical briefsSkip for now
Skincare + hairCleanser, SPF, shampoo, hair oilRoutine, texture, GRWMClinical claims you cannot back
Home + kitchenMug, candle, dish soap, air fryerReset clips, recipe insertsFull interior design sets
Tech + deskEarbuds, charger, laptop standUnbox, problem/resultGaming PCs you do not have
Food + drinkCoffee, sauce, snacksFirst bite, pour, pack-in-bagRestaurant-level plating
Fitness + wellnessMat, bottle, protein, vitaminsHabit clips, no medical claimsSupplement before/after body shots

Walk your place once and tick products from the everyday product checklist. Two categories is enough. One category only makes you look like you can do a single brief type.

Once the eight files exist, the slow part is getting them in front of a buyer. A short pitch with three clips attached gets read. newcollab writes the email and attaches your kit.

Film 8 Samples This Weekend

Use the same setup for every product so you are not rebuilding lights eight times. After the first two, each clip takes about 10 minutes to shoot.

Saturday morning: setup and first four

  1. Face a window. Turn off mixed overhead lights. A $20 tripod or a mug at eye level beats handheld for the whole video.
  2. Wipe labels and the surface. Brands need the product readable for at least one second.
  3. Record 9:16, lock exposure by tapping the screen. Do not switch to horizontal "just this once."
  4. For each product, shoot four pieces: 3s hook, 2-4s label insert, 8-15s use, 3-5s close.

Saturday afternoon: the other four

Change rooms if you can (bathroom, kitchen, desk) so the folder does not look like one wall. Keep talking. Silent texture clips help. Keep your voice on at least half the files.

Sunday: edit and name files

  • Cut dead air. Add captions. Keep 15-30 seconds.
  • Leave the watermark off. Export 1080x1920 MP4.
  • Name files so a stranger can scan the folder: 01-cleanser-talking-head.mp4, 02-cleanser-texture.mp4.
  • Pick the best eight. Delete the rest from the share folder. You can keep rejects in a private archive.
BlockWhat you finishOutput
Sat 9-12Setup + 4 products, talking-head + useRaw clips in camera roll
Sat 1-44 more products, including 2 silent B-rollRaw clips
Sun 10-1Edit 8 files, captions, exportMP4s on your laptop
Sun 1-2Upload Drive + newcollab, write 3-line pitchShareable folder

Quality Checklist Before You Send

Open each file once on your phone with the sound on. If you skip this, the brand will do it for you and you will not get the reply.

CheckPassFail
Product readableLogo or label in frame, in focusBottle in shadow or cropped
First 3 secondsA problem or a clear visual of the product"Hey guys welcome back" then 8 seconds of nothing
AudioYour voice, room is quiet enoughMusic you cannot license, or kitchen fan drowning you
LightFace and product both visibleBacklit silhouette, yellow overhead only
Length15-30 seconds90 seconds with a long intro
FileMP4, 9:16, no watermarkTikTok save with username burned in
One ideaOne product, one claimFull 10-step routine in one video
It sounds like youYou would say this to a friendScript you would not say out loud in a shop

If three files fail more than two rows, reshoot those three. Do not send the whole folder "to show range."

How to Package and Share the Folder

Brands will not log into five tools. One Drive (or Dropbox) link set to "anyone with the link can view" is enough. Put a one-line readme at the top of the folder.

Folder layout

ItemExample
Folder nameYourName_UGC_Portfolio_2026
ReadmeREADME.txt with niche, location, email, and that files are watermark-free
ClipsEight MP4s, numbered, product in the filename
Optional PDFOne-page media kit. Same name as you.

What to write when you send it

Three lines. Product category, what is in the folder, and a clear ask.

  • Line 1: "I make vertical UGC for skincare and home. Eight watermark-free samples: [link]."
  • Line 2: "Best starting points: 01-cleanser and 05-candle. Both 20 seconds, captions on."
  • Line 3: "I can turn a brief in 5-7 days. Rates on the PDF in the same folder."

Attach the one-page media kit if you have it. If you do not, send the clips anyway. Footage first.

If you do not want to hunt emails one by one, put the same eight files on a newcollab creator profile. Brands that already pay for UGC are listed here.

Mistakes That Get Portfolios Skipped

MistakeWhat the brand doesFix
20+ files, no orderClicks one, leavesEight files, numbered, best two called out in the email
Only selfies, no product insertCannot see the SKUAdd a 2-second label shot to every talking-head
Trending audio onlyCannot license it for adsYour voice, or a commercial library track
Horizontal videoDoes not fit Stories/TikTok/Reels adsReshoot 9:16. Cropping a wide video looks worse.
"I can film anything"Sounds like no nicheName two categories you already filmed
Watermarked TikTok savesUnusable in paid mediaExport from the editor with no username
Google Drive set to request accessThey will not request itAnyone with the link can view
One 4-minute vlog as the "portfolio"They need ads, not a vlogCut it into 20-second product clips

If you want gifted product later, the same samples work for PR pitches. The companies that send PR packages list is a separate path from paid UGC.

FAQ

How many videos do I need in a UGC portfolio?

Eight clean clips is enough to start pitching. Twelve is better if you cover two categories, for example skincare and home. Three strong 20-second videos beat a folder of 20 messy ones.

Do I need a website or a paid portfolio tool?

No. A Google Drive folder with view access, plus a newcollab profile, is what most UGC managers open. A Notion page or a simple link-in-bio is extra, not required.

Can I use products I bought myself?

Yes. Sample videos of products you already own are how most creators get the first paid brief. Do not pretend the brand hired you. Paid work usually ships the real product after you are booked.

Is a UGC portfolio the same as a media kit?

No. The portfolio is the video samples. The media kit is a one-pager with rates, niche, and contact. Send both. If you only have time for one, send the clips first. Brands hire from footage.

Should I post every sample on TikTok or Instagram?

You do not have to. Keep watermark-free MP4s in Drive. Public posts help if they already perform, but brands cannot run ads with your handle burned in, so always keep a clean file.

How long should each UGC sample be?

15 to 30 seconds, vertical 9:16, captions on, 1080p, no watermark. Brands trim longer files anyway. If a brief asks for 45 or 60 seconds later, you already have the shot style they can brief against.
